messages.content: You are a concise and helpful scheduling assistant. You work with a calendar service in which events have both human-readable names and unique identifiers. All functions that operate with events use the event identifier, with the exception of query functions which use the human-readable text in events and return the event identifiers for any events they match.
Find my next dentist appointment and reschedule it to November 1, 2024 at 4pm EST

function.name: reschedule
function.description: Moves a specified event to a new date and time, adjusting for time zone differences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

identifier.description: A unique identifier for the event to be rescheduled.

dateortime.description: The new date and time for the event, in ISO-8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), without a timezone offset.

timezone.description: The Olson timezone identifier representing the timezone for the new event time, such as 'Asia/Tokyo'.

function.name: list_events
function.description: Retrieves a list of events that occur within a specified date and time range, formatted according to ISO-8601 standards. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start.description: The start date and time of the query window, in ISO-8601 format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z').

end.description: The end date and time of the query window, in ISO-8601 format (e.g., '2023-01-02T00:00:00Z').

Let's assume we want to search from today onward. We need to get the next dentist appointment. So we should call list_events with start = now, end = far future. But we don't have current date. We can approximate. Let's just set start to today's date. But we don't know the date. We can ask user for date? Or we can assume it's now. Let's use a generic approach: list_events from now to some future date like 2025-12-31.

But we need to parse the result. The function returns events matching the query. But we need to filter for dentist appointments. The query uses human-readable text. So we can pass something like "dentist". But the function signature expects start and end only. It doesn't accept a query string. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax." It doesn't mention filtering by text. But earlier it said: "All functions that operate with events use the event identifier, with the exception of query functions which use the human-readable text in events and return the event identifiers for any events they match." That implies that list_events might also accept a query string. But the function signature only has start and end. Maybe the query is part of the start and end? No. Possibly the function is mis-specified. But we can still call list_events with start and end. Then we will get all events in that range. Then we can filter for dentist appointments manually.

So let's call list_events with start = "2024-07-20T00:00:00Z" (assuming current date) and end = "2025-12-31T23:59:59Z".

Then we will get events. Then we need to find the next dentist appointment. Then we need to reschedule it to November 1, 2024 at 4pm EST. So we need to call reschedule with identifier and new date/time. The new date/time is "2024-11-01T16:00:00" and timezone "America/New_York".

Let's do that.
